Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What shocked you last week?
Answer: The police came to my door. Asked me if it was true that I had the key to my neighbor’s house. I said I did. They then asked me if I would please open her door for them — they had been called by one of her friends and were alarmed by what she had said. So I did. The whole house was dark. All curtains were drawn. She was on the sofa, on the edge, it’s a large sofa shaped like the letter L. A blanket draped on her. Yes, she was breathing. Turned her head really slowly but wasn’t really seeing anything. She was drowsy. There were medicine wrappers on her lap and on the floor. She tried to kill herself. And she didn’t succeed, because she had called a former partner right before she took the pills. When I entered the room, followed by the police, she recognized me. And said my name. There was a strange tone in her voice. Almost one of betrayal. I’m conflicted, now. Did she want to die, and did she hate the fact that I interrupted her? Or did she send those dramatic text messages with the explicit desire for the police or someone else to come to her rescue? I’m still not sure. It could be an elaborate cry for attention. It could also be a genuine desire for help. It could be both suicidal ideation and desperation, both, at once. The morning she made her suicide attempt, she had been in my house. This same neighbor. Drunk, crying, at eight o’clock in the morning. Telling me she’ll never be a mother, a grandmother, that her life is “effectively over” and asking me what’s the point. She has given me the same exact talk before. Nothing about it made it feel different, this time around. But it was. Because she took an overdose that same day. An ambulance took her away and I haven’t seen her since.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the darkest cartoon conspiracies?
Answer: There’s one theory people always seem to talk about online. It’s become somewhat of a meme, but it’s quite dark. It speculates the main character of Pokémon, Ash, is in a coma… he’s fantasizing about a magical world where he’s travelling around with his buddy Pikachu, an electrically charge mouse-like creature. He battles other magical creatures. Everything is bright and fun and every day brings another brand new adventure. Only it’s all a lie… there are no magical creatures. There are no adventures. Not for him anymore, anyway. All there is for Ash are the machines keeping him alive. Liquids going in and out of him, preventing organ failure. No one talks to him but his crying mother. Pikachu doesn’t exist — and why would he, he’s a yellow upright-walking mouse that endlessly repeats his own name… where on earth could such a ridiculous creature exist but in the fever dreams of a comatose Japanese kid who watched one too many weird anime shows? It’s kind of a cop-out. Very unfulfilling. Dark. Shows do it sometimes when a strange sequence takes place, shocking or unbelievable things happen — at the end of the episode, or at the beginning of the next, they have the main character wake up and go: “Oh, it was all just a dream, how silly!” Only in this theory, the dream now is the reality. And Ash will never leave the hospital alive to find out it is all a lie.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What’s the biggest double life you’ve ever personally seen revealed?
Answer: Here’s a photo from the 1990s of a man called Josef Fritzl, vacationing in Thailand without a care in the world. Fritzl was a businessman, married, father of seven, from Austria. He’d frequently travel the world. One year he’d be in Thailand. Another year he’d go to Africa. At times his friends would join him, they would drink, swim, lounge around resorts and float in the swimming pools of resorts… Fritzl was a doting grandfather of twenty. Three of his grandchildren lived with him and his wife — his youngest daughter Elizabeth, their mother, had ran away from home and joined a cult. So Fritzl and his wife raised their grandchildren. By all means, Josef had a charmed life. What no one knew? The three grandchildren he was raising were also his own biological children… their mother Elizabeth hadn’t joined a “cult”, she lived in a dungeon Fritzl had built inside his own basement. With three other children Fritzl also fathered there by his own daughter. Fritzl was arrested in 2008, at the age of 73. Because he had brought one of the “dungeon kids” to the hospital along with Elizabeth, his captive daughter, who then alerted authorities. Josef Fritzl remains in prison in Austria of this writing. He believes he should be freed, famously telling a judge: “I am just one man. But look inside the basements of other people… you would be surprised what you find!”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What, in your opinion, is the greatest government conspiracy or cover-up in history, and why?
Answer: In 2018, Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was brutally murdered inside the Saudi embassy in Istanbul, Turkey. Mr. Kashoggi was rather critical of the Saudi government, in particular of its de-facto leader, Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Salman (MBS). Many people think this is the only reason the journalist was killed. But the story goes… a little deeper. What few looked into is the particular story Mr. Khashoggi was working on at the time of his murder — it had to do with Jared Kushner, son-in-law of then US president Trump. Khashoggi had unearthed a connection between the two men… Kushner had been selling classified documents to the Saudi’s, and MBS used the information thus acquired to rid himself of rivals within Saudi Arabia. Some were arrested, some had ‘mysterious’ and awfully convenient helicopter crashes… After Trump left the White House following his 2020 presidential defeat, Kushner received an investment of 2 billion(!) dollars to his equity firm. With Kushner, himself, overseeing the money.[1] This was the blood money he received. The value of his silence, his cooperation. And this lucrative partnership and the priceless information thus acquired, is why Khashoggi had to go… The American government was quick to label the murder of Khashoggi “an outrage” but little else happened. Because they knew exactly what the man was up to, and why he had to go. Jared Kushner sold state secrets and classified information to the tune of billions, and the man about to expose him was chainsawed to pieces while still alive for it. And “certain people” do NOT want you to know about this, for obvious reasons.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are most black women unattractive?
Answer: How foolish of you. You’ve obviously never seen Michael Jackson’s music video for “Remember The Time” starring Somali super model Iman, have you? I did. I was just a kid. But you may say, in a sense, it made me a man. My first celebrity crushes had been white or middle eastern women. And this video opened my eyes to the beauty of Africa. She exudes CLASS, in her every pore. Her jawline, her nose, divine. Her eye shape, her eyebrows. That skin, so flawless, so smooth… and of course her body is amazing, too. Those eyes… Iman, for the record, married David Bowie. Another man of culture. He recognized that beauty. Wasn’t blind to it, and what man ever could be? They made a gorgeous couple. Stayed together until he died of cancer. Still miss that brilliant man. Just recently, I fell in love with an African girl, myself. She’s from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. And she’s absolutely gorgeous, too. Even her handwriting is pretty — she wrote me a letter, and scanned it and sent me a copy of the photograph. And her voice, too. On video calls, it’s like some dream sequence where I’m talking to an Angel come to earth. Yeah, I know. I sound corny. But that’s how love works, isn’t it? She’s just so damn regal. And no, I know — not every African girl is regal, and gorgeous, and a super model. But plenty of them are absolutely stunning. Every ethnic group, every race and nationality has it’s good and less good-looking members. Me, I’ve never been able to deny the allure of ebony. I understand perfectly why King Solomon fell for the Queen of Sheba.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are the benefits of facial recognition?
Answer: A lesbian dating app made headlines in June 2024 for using facial recognition software to exclude transgender women.[1] There had been an issue with women using the app complaining about transgender (male-to-female) women chatting them up, sometimes refusing to disclose their status as former men. The dating app claims to be able to “clock” a male-to-female transgender with supposedly 100% certainty. I suppose this would count as a benefit — it makes it harder for people to hide the truth from others. I can only hope the same software will soon be applied to those who use filters, or makeup. And show the “real you” even when you try desperately to hide it. To prevent disappointment, people really should be straight-forward about this sort of thing. As in all things, honesty is the best policy. Too many people hide who they truly are — their gender, the appearance, what their actual face looks like without makeup, or they hide their weight by posting old photos or photos that are neck-up only. When it comes to dating and online catfishes, AI might just save the day!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is there a long history of women being targeted in India?
Answer: If we strictly look at statistics for a moment and forget about fearmongering and sensationalism for just a minute… we find that there are several countries with a higher percentage of rapes and sexual assaults per percentage of population than India.[1] We find, for instance, that 27% of Chinese women who are married or in a relationship have experienced physical or sexual violence.[2] There’s this knee-jerk response in much of the world — they think of India, and they immediately think of a nation of perverts that defecate in the streets. It’s a grossly racist depiction, and it doesn’t hold up in terms of statistics. Because sure enough, Indian women are victimized on a daily basis. They are raped, assaulted, injured and have their honor besmirched by nasty creatures… but the same happens to women everywhere else, the world over. Even prosperous Sweden has a Sweden has 63.50 rape rate and around 5,960 incidents in per 100,000 citizens, to name another example… but Swedes aren’t stereotyped as a nation of rapists, last I checked. Nor are Chinese, or Jamaicans, or Americans. And yet in all these nations, sexual violence is rampant. Truth be told — India does not have a “special history” of women being targetted. Not anymore than other countries. India is both a huge country with 1.4 billion inhabitants, and a country that hasn’t outlawed protests. So when a high profile rape case happens in India, tens of thousands of angry women take to the streets. In China the same rape could happen but the protest would never take place or spread, because the state wouldn’t allow it. And in the West, all you’ll see is some performative celebrity outrage, but no tangible policy changes.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Have any of the Republican’s line of attacks stuck against Vice President Kamala Harris?
Answer: The most nasty accusation thrown at Kamala Harris by Trump and his followers is that she “slept her way to the top”. There is some truth to the rumor, too. In the early 1990s, Harris had a brief relationship with San Francisco mayor Willie Brown, a man several decades her senior. Kamala’s own career was only just taking off in those days, and Brown was a powerful man in local politics. Did her dalliance with Brown help Harris, politically? It certainly can’t have hurt her, career-wise. The “diversity hire” accusation backfired with likely voters as it was deemed ‘racist’ by quite a few people in the public. But the “sleeping your way to the top” argument is fairly effective when there are actually pictures out there of a young, remarkably pretty Kamala Harris hanging on to the arm of a wealthy politician old enough to be her father. It’s kind of a low blow, especially coming from Trump, a man who famously would bang a refridgerator if you put lipstick on it and a blonde wig and told him it was made in Eastern Europe. There’s also the “Kamala Harris was in charge of the border” line of attack — this one kind of backfired when the Harris team kept pointing out that there was a bipartisan border bill that Republicans nuked at the behest of Trump, specifically so he could keep hammering immigration as a talking point for the November elections. So they’re stuck with “Kamala has a weird nervous laugh” and “she slept her way to power”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some mind-blowing facts about Ukraine?
Answer: Here’s a scary fact about Ukraine — it has a fertility rate that may be the second-lowest in the world.[1] The year before Russia’s 2022 invasion, the fertility rate of Ukraine stood at around 1.1 child per woman. By now, it’s at about 0.7 child per woman. By contast, the country with the lowest fertility rate in the world, South Korea, is at about 0.65 child per woman. In other words… war or no war, Ukraine is dying out. By contrast, Russia’s fertility rate is hovering around 1.5, which is low enough for Russian officials to practically beg Russian mothers to have more babies.[2] The situation is dire for Russia already. And yet, Ukraine’s women have about 50% fewer children than Russian women. And even before the war broke out, their numbers were already significantly worse... A nation without a young generation to take over, is a nature without a future. Yes, it’s bleak. But why lie and beat around the bush with pointless coping mechanisms and mental gymnastics? Ukraine is in an incredibly rough spot and has been for decades with no end in sight. One of the most mind-blowing and tragic facts about Ukraine is that it’s a nation that was already in a very dark place long before the Russian invasion. It was plagued by scandals, corrupt officials, and it’s people were in a hopeless situation. Now they’re fighting for their lives, and fighting valiantly. But few people seem aware of just how dire things have been for Ukraine, and how much worse they are, now.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did Quora have any impact on your life? Did you get any new perspectives that helped you in your life
Answer: One interesting connection I made was with a young Filipino man who was part of a cult. I wrote about our connection in another answer, years ago. He was faced with a devilish dilemma — either leave his fiancé of several years, or persuade her to join the cult for him. She didn’t want to, and he didn’t really want to make her do it. But if he didn’t, her eternal soul would be forfeit. And if he left, so would his. He wrestled with this moral dilemma for years as he remained loyal to the INC (Iglesia ni Cristo). He came to me for some advice on the matter. We talked. And talked. And talked. We talked for weeks. And finally he came to see my point of view — that true love means you would never force someone to switch faiths just to make things “easier” on you. He also came to realize, and accept for himself at long last, that the church he was part of was, indeed, a cult. It controlled what he spent money on, what he ate, drank, even controlled his political votes because the church leaders would get bribed by politicians and would then tell all cult members to “vote in unison” because “unison is Biblical”… I swear, you cannot make this shit up. Through our conversations he came to finally see and accept the absurdity of his faith. And decided to leave once and for all. His parents, sadly, were penalized for this and lost some standing in the community; that’s another way a cult can hold its wayward members emotionally hostage. In 2022, my friend and his lady, on their way to marriage, invited me to a nice resort in Boracay, the Philippines. They treated me to nice food, to island hopping by boat, snorkeling and endless buffets. He was a free man, now. Grateful for my help. We’re still in touch, every now and then. Quora gave me friends for life, and one of the best vacation I’ve ever had!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Whos your favorite athlete of all time?
Answer: For me, it’s Mike Tyson. Not just because of how he dominated the ring. Not just for his sheer brutality, the force of nature that he is. But for the enigma of a person that Tyson is. There’s a lot of lived experience within him. There’s wisdom, too. One Tyson quote often replays in my head: “A man who is a friend to everybody is an enemy to himself.” That’s a beautiful quote. And it’s true — you CANNOT be kind and friendly and a friend to everyone, because you’ll get walked over and you’ll lose yourself in the process. Another fine Tyson quote that’s worthwhile: “Everyone that you fight is not your enemy and everyone who helps you is not your friend.” And then there’s another that lives rent-free in my head. This one isn’t particularly deep, it’s just hilarious as far as social commentary goes. Tyson on social media: "Social media made y'all way too comfortable with disrespecting people and not getting punched in the face for it." On top of these quotes, his little insights into life and how he sees it… he’s pretty damn hilarious, too. Loved Mike Tyson in the Hangover movie. He’s pretty much the best part of it. Primarily because if anyone in the world would have a pet tiger, get it stolen and be super chill about the whole thing as long as it’s returned to him? It’d be him. Because he’s kind of wild like that. Mike Tyson. Another quote, to end it all with: If I have to live at the top of the world, I also have to live at the bottom of the ocean. I don't know how to live in the middle of life." Mike Tyson, who could not live in the middle of life. Who made and blew tens of millions of dollars over the years. Who was on top of the world, and on the very bottom. And needed to see, experience and feel it all. Have, win, and lose it all. To be who he is, now.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why are leftists so angry about Project 2025? The way I see it, it will eliminate corruption and put America back on the right track. Are leftists just afraid they will lose their grip on power?
Answer: They aren’t angry… they’re scared. Project 2025 is a collection of proposals by the “Heritage Foundation”, a conservative far-right think tank. It seeks to do many of the things right-wing politicians and the billionaires backing them have wanted to do for decades. Only it is far more organized than ever before. Project 2025 believes “cultural marxism” has infiltrated the school system. To rectify this, it seeks to abolish the department of education altogether. Project 2025 wants to stop the “LGBT propaganda” in schools. Teach children that family values are most important, that morality matters and that there are only two genders — male and female. It places God at the center of the world, back into houses and classrooms. It promotes traditional values. But it does something else. Something other conservative think tanks never managed to do… Project 2025 made a list of potential public servants and judges to be appointed. Tens of thousands of possible candidates. And it seeks to replace the entire government with loyalists, if Trump wins in 2024. Meaning that NO candidate who isn’t fully on board with extremely conservative Evangelical christianity could ever be appointed to so much as sweep the floor in a post-2025 government. America has long had a tradition of “picking the best man/woman for the job”. At least there was this illusion of impartiality. Project 2025 pulled off the mask, and stopped pretending — it wants the government to be filled and ran, top to bottom, with yes-men who will rubber-stamp and sign any proposal put before it. This, combined with a Supreme Court that already leans far to the right and presidential powers and immunity greatly enhanced, will essentially turn America into a Christian nationalist theocracy.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Does a man of God need to work?
Answer: The finest priests I have known were men’s men. They weren’t afraid to roll up their sleeves and get down and dirty when they needed to. They would give a sermon in different communities — some of them quite remote. And they would get on their motorcycles and cross rough terrain, climb mountains, brave rough weather conditions, just to speak the word of the Lord to those people. Who do you think builds the churches in faraway places? It’s priests like this. These priests, they didn’t have clean hands. They were rough, calloused. In the evening after a hard day’s work, tending to the ill, comforting the dying, joining festivities and funeral rites… they would have a drink. Some brandy, for courage. A late night call would call them away from bed, once more. Someone nearing the end, in need of solace. Finally, bed. Rest. Sleep. Only a few hours, and at the breaking of dawn, another brutal day… Yes, a man of God needs to work, if he’s any good at his job, he’ll work like a mule and still get complaints and criticism all around. There are priests who are abusive, lazy, nasty, decadent… their clothes are perfectly fitting, clean, tidy, just as their rooms are. And they’re not “Godly” at all. The best priests and pastors are simple, hard-working men. Like Jesus, the carpenter. Hard men with soft souls.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How have you experienced or witnessed societal obsession with fair skin?
Answer: For years I lived in the Philippines and the national obsession seemed to be how fair one’s skin was. Skin whitening products were everywhere. Special soaps, special shampoos, all designed to keep the skin light as possible or lighten it further. Women and young girls would wear little umbrellas on sunny days wherever they went out to keep their skins light. It didn’t help, of course, that 90% of all the models, actors and actresses were mixed race — they virtually all had at least one white parent or grandparent. Others may have a particularly light-skinned father from the Arab world. But few were “pure Filipino”. Aside from white skin, European features were seen as perfect. A “tall nose” as opposed to a “flat nose”. Large, expressive eyes, as opposed to small beady eyes. Some naturally had a lighter skin and more European features even without having a foreign parent or grandparent; but it is fairly rare. The legacy of colonialism comes into play as well, with quite a few Filipinos having Spanish, Chinese or American ancestors. Above all else, light skin was the number one obsession. It trumped everything. There was one girl in our neighborhood who had a plain face, but very fair skin. She was considered far more attractive than her sister, whose face was gorgeous but noticeably darker. When I had a son with a Filipina mestiza in 2023 he came out pale with blonde hair, green eyes, a pointed nose — the whole hospital freaked out and obsessed over him. Random strangers still obsess over him.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who are some famous intellectual badasses?
Answer: It is quite hard not to admire Mark Twain. The man was incredibly clever and skilled in deconstructing damaging narratives and social constructions… everyone always speaks of the now-controversial “Huckleberry Finn”, but he also wrote another great book — the now shamefully forgotten Pudd'nhead Wilson. In Pudd'nhead Wilson, Mark Twain takes apart the “one drop rule” myth of black ancestry, and does so beautifully… two boys are mixed at birth, one fully white, the other of distant black ancestry. Twain dives into things like scientific racism, racial superioty, all themes incredibly controversial for his day and age — his Pudd’nhead Wilson was published in 1894. Huckleberry Finn was published ten years earlier, in 1884. And there, too, he deconstructed myths and humanized a part of the population (black people, former slaves) that too many in society saw as “lesser”. Above we see Twain with his best friend, a former slave named John T. Lewis on whom he based some of his black characters. I would label Mr. Twain every inch the “intellectual badass”. If only for amazing quotes such as: “Censorship is telling a man he can't have a steak just because a baby can't chew it.” Or: “If voting made a difference, they wouldn’t let us do it!” Mark Twain was the sort of no-nonsense, straightforward, razor-sharp wit that comes around perhaps once a century, if even that. He was the real deal. And he didn’t give a damn about what society thought of him — he was the very rarest of creatures: honest, genuine and true intellect expressed with eloquence unmatched.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is President Trump the new Theodore Roosevelt?
Answer: Don’t be ridiculous. Theodore Roosevelt was a 250 pound mountain of self-made muscle who gave a speech, got shot into the chest and, spitting out blood with a smile, told the alarmed crowd: “It takes more than that to kill a bull moose!” He then proceeded to give his speech anyway as if nothing had happened. It’s the type of scene that would make people roll their eyes in an anime series and say: “Gee, those Japanese cartoons sure are over-the-top bombastic and unbelievable!” When Theodore Roosevelt was born, he was weak and sickly. Doctors said he’d surely die. His father believed otherwise. As soon as his son was old enough to understand, he told him: “God gave you a strong mind, but not a strong body. So you must build that body yourself.” He nodded and internalized that message. Started a fitness regimen of insane intensity, including calisthenics and bodyweight exercises. He climbed mountains. Fought in multiple wars. Knocked down several men at a time in bar fights, and rode horses and trekked through the roughest of terrain. His band of men was called “the Rough Riders”. About as close as a 19th century politician could be to being in a biker gang… When Theodore Roosevelt was nearly assassinated he survived with a bullet lodged in his chest for the rest of his life. It did not, in any way, shape or form, slow the man down. His very first concern, after telling the crowd he was fine, was for the would-be assassin — he told police not to rough him up too bad. If the shooter had merely nicked his ear, Roosevelt would probably have asked him to come up close and said: “Mediocre! Come, have another go!”

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do you assess the arrest of Telegram's boss Pavel Durov by French intelligence services?
Answer: It sets a dangerous precedent. Because think of Mr. Durov whatever you want, Telegram as a service has value. It allowed revolutionaries to plan protests from Iran to Hong Kong, allowed freedom of speech to occur even under oppressive regimes… Honestly? I kind of love Telegram, its flaws notwithstanding. When Hong Kongers stood up in enormous numbers to Chinese oppression, it was Telegram that allowed them when other apps and communication channels had been breached. When Iranian women stood up to their brutal government, it was Telegram they used to plan it all… I say the guy who facilitated all that is a pretty swell dude, if for that fact alone. Now there are issues, of course — real, genuine issues. Some of the content floating around Telegram is questionable, to say the least. And not everyone on the site has noble intentions. It has criminals, too. Drug dealers. Even pedophiles. And I agree wholeheartedly with French authorities that the app ought to make more of an effort to remove such nasty elements and cooperate with law enforcement in such matters… But to arrest the CEO and actually float around the idea of banning Telegram altogether? That’s ain’t it, chief. I don’t like Durov particularly much. Nor am I fond of Zuckerberg or Musk. In fact all three of them are odious in their own unique ways. But I still love freedom of speech more than I dislike any of them. And I always will.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why does America always involve itself in warfare?
Answer: You know how much money the American defense industry made in 2023 alone? An astonishing 298.68 billion(!) dollars. It’s a business. The late great President Eisenhower referred to it as the “military industrial complex”. America has 1000+ military bases around the world. People have to be flown in or sailed in. They have to be trained, armed, equipped. It’s enormously costly. Virtually all major trade routes in the world, are controlled and patrolled by American troops. You can throw a rock anywhere in the world and if you throw it far enough, chances are you’ll hit an American military vehicle or a soldier. It’s a lucrative business. And it has led to a world order in which America, largely, calls the shots. Sure, Russia will pretend otherwise. China will huff and puff like the big bad wolf… but none can blow apart the fortress America has been building steadily over the last century or so. America helped defeat Nazi Germany. Saw the rise of the Soviets and decided… “Nope, we’re not going to allow that.” Rather than allow other empires to build up steam, the American military decided to make itself the biggest, the most powerful in the world. All other potential rivals have been playing catch-up ever since — and as of 2024, none come even remotely close to taking over the spot of Top Dog.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is President Trump one of the toughest men alive today?
Answer: You know who are tough? Firemen. Like Mr. Corey Comperatore who was shot and killed a week ago. He would run into burning buildings to save people’s lives. He’d get burned, he’d be covered in smoke as far as the eye could see and still would keep going. It’s one of those jobs that takes a lot out of a man. You put your life on the line, day and night, to save the lives of others. At any hour of the night the call can come — and you’ll jump out of bed and, within a minute, are on your way to the fire station. No time to rest, no time to wake up properly or contemplate the risks involved. You just, go. No hesitation. Never hesitation. Corey Comperatore was such a man. And Corey Comperatore was the man who caught the bullet meant for Donald J. Trump at his rally. You want to call the 78-year-old pampered son of a New York real estate tycoon “tough” because his ear got nicked by a sniper? A 78-year-old philandering billionaire draft dodger and a conman? Don’t make me laugh. A lion died so a worm could live.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What actor/actress is easy to love?
Answer: There’s something about a man like Jack Black. It must be freeing to be so unapologetically yourself, all the times. The man doesn’t give a shit. Yes, he’s fat. He has a beard like Karl Marx just had a baby with a Bronze Age cavewoman and it was raised in the mean streets of Moscow. And he doesn’t care. He just doesn’t. At no point does the guy pretend to be better than he is, more than he is. It’s just a vibe, I suppose. An aura. There are men who have to do a ton of charity stuff to be liked, to come across as likable, wonderful. People who have to make real effort to be seen a certain way… and it just kind of happens, with Jack Black. He walks into a room and you’re entertained. Instantly. He’s not a dumb guy. Could have been anything. He’s a musician, he’s an actor. His mother was literally in NASA and created the guidance system that saved the Apollo 13 astronauts. But he won’t brag about it. Won’t brag about a damn thing. No, he’ll just crack jokes at his own expense. Be his worst or his finest self. It’s a quality I also see in men like Danny DeVito. Jack Black’s kinda like DeVito, only 3D-printed to 1.3 times the size of the former. It’s to love a guy like Jack Black. Sometimes he’s a little “too much” but, I don’t know. He just sort of makes me happy. I’m glad he exists in this world. Puts a smile on my face that he’s here.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What are some 'recent' things that are actually older than people realize?
Answer: One thing that is far, far older than we realize — the selfie. On the picture below we see Russian Tsar Nicholas II taking a selfie in the year 1896. It looks surprisingly modern, were it not for the lack of color and the military uniform. Nicholas II was modern in several other ways, too —for one, he was a major fitness buff and in incredibly good shape. Another thing many people don’t know is that he was covered in tattoos. He had one particularly large tattoo on his arm, that he got together with his royal relative, the future British King George V, when they visited Japan together in 1882. If I spoke to you today about a man who had tattoos, who was a fitness freak with a dragon tattoo on his arm, taking selfies… you’d think he must have been born in this century or the previous one. You wouldn’t expect it from a man born in Russia in 1868.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Did Tsar Nicolas II deserve his fate during the Russian Revolution of 1917?
Answer: Had the Soviets properly put Tsar Nicholas II on trial and executed him after, they may have had a point. But they didn’t… they bayonetted and shot to death the Tsar. And not just the Tsar, but also his children. There really is no excuse for this. Just, look at them. They’re adorable. What sort of absolute animals would shoot, stab and bludgeon to death a whole family just because their father happened to be head of state of a rather repressive state? It’s the kind of historical cruelty that simply boggles the mind. People always repeat the same old mantra… “Orders are orders!” they say. And sure, orders are orders. But does that justify anything, really? I can definitely see how a revolution may take place, and the former leaders of the country are put on trial and executed. Allowing the nation to start anew with a clean slate. But the children? Such needless brutality. It is unforgivable. The argument that “the Romanovs may have rallied in exile and tried to return!” is nonsense, too — many dynasties have fallen, and its members were allowed to live. The Last Emperor of China, Puyi, was allowed to live out his days as a simple gardener in Communist China. The state used this forgiveness towards him as a propaganda tool. Tsar Nicholas II wasn’t a bad man, as far as monarchs in his era go. He was far less militaristic than the Kaiser, for instance, who loved the army to almost fetishistic levels. In some ways, Nicholas was even a reformer. The Soviets could have allowed the man into exile. Or could have even kept him around and tried to use him and his family as propaganda tools, the way the Chinese later did with Puyi. Brutal murder was the most stupid and short-sighted “solution” to the Romanov problem.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the most disturbing image you saw today?
Answer: A man named Homer Peel kisses his wife, Geneva Peel, in 1937. She was just ten years old, and an oprhan. Peel lied to authorities initially and told them Geneva was twelve… child marriage had just been made illegal in the state of Tennessee — but Homer Peel claimed he had “saved” Geneva from the poor house, and that to annul the marriage would be to return her to a state of poverty. The picture above is Homer kissing Geneva after a judge agreed them his reasoning, refusing to undo the marriage and returning Geneva to her husband, twenty-four years older than her. He had reportedly “promised her a pretty new hat” for her loyaly. It was quite common in the 1930s for children to marry… they would typically marry men considerably older than them. It wasn’t until 1937 that a law prohibiting it came into existence, and even then, the practice continued. The photograph is jarring and unsettling for numerous reasons. Homer and Geneva Peel entually stayed together until 1975, when they got divorced. Homer died in 1991 and Geneva lived on until 2017, dying at 92. The couple had six daughters and a son together, and eighteen grandchildren.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How can I get better in bed?
Answer: It’s incredibly simple. Be fit. Everything becomes more enjoyable when you’re fit. But especially night-time bedroom gymnastics. Be fit, so you have the strength, stamina and flexibility to go that extra mile. To switch positions and play naked Twister games like a champion. To really go out of your way and excel. There’s hardly any sexual problem in the world that cannot be achieved by eating healthier food and building healthier habits. For the men — drink a lot of water, and take vitamin supplements, especially those that contain zinc. Make sure at least 10% of all the food you consume daily consists of protein. You are what you eat. And you become how you live. If you want every part of yourself to be at its finest condition, you have to care for yourself the way you would care for a million dollar race horse. Too many of us are kinder to antique chairs or collectible items we own than we are to our own bodies. Hence, we deteriorate.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is feminism about hating men?
Answer: Not by design, no. It’s actually fairly straight-forward — feminism is about equal rights. At least on paper, that is. That doesn’t mean people don’t get… carried away. And that some feminists aren’t constantly talking about how awful men are. Because they do. It’s all many of them online talk about. They can’t form a proper sentence without throwing the word ‘men’ in it or ‘patriarchy’. Like a Pokémon repeating its own name. A lot of online activism is centered around the concept that “not all men are bad but all men benefit from the actions of bad men”. They have created this fantasy world in which any man who isn’t speaking out every second of every day about how awful women have it and how awful other men are, is somehow inherently “complicit” in this mythical beast called “the patriarchy”. As a result, modern day feminism is incredibly toxic. And it’s also incredibly performative, and fake. I should know this — I had a brief little love affair with a young feminist. And yes, she was lost alright. Personal issues drove her to say the things she said and half the time, she didn’t even truly feel that way… she just wanted the other e-activists to suck her proverbial dong for saying outrageously anti-men things. She eventually made a big deal out of wanting to come across as impartial, but it never quite worked. A lot of her more aggressive outbursts came from a place of anger, of being fundamentally broken on some level. She was fascinating. Complex. And a lost soul, like any of us. And that’s kind of how it always goes, isn’t it? In any movement for equality or ‘fairness’, the other gender or the other race or the other group that is ‘privileged’ lives rent-free in your head. You obsess over them. Because the “bad men” and the “bad women”, the “misogynist” and the “rabid feminist” are all the dual sides of a single coin. They need each other. Modern feminism needs bad men. And it needs all men to be bad as much as a medieval pope needs all women to be guilty of Eve’s love of apples.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why was Tim Walz's tampon bill controversial?
Answer: The bill Minnesota governor Tim Walz proposed stipulated all schools in the state to keep a stock of tampons for female students who would have their periods. He felt feminine products should be freely available, the way toilet paper is. This seems like a pretty sensible and perfectly reasonable stance to take. Now here’s where it gets weird, to use one of the favorite words of Mr. Walz — schools were required to keep tampons not only in female bathrooms (which would have been perfectly reasonable) but in the boys bathrooms as well. Of course boys don’t menstruate. Unless maybe it’s a transgender (girk-to-boy) pupil. Of which there are very, very few. Like, my own daughters go to a fairly large school. Haven’t seen a single “trans kid”. So yeah that’s a bit odd. Still? It’s one of those stories where the issue being decried is what I would call a “victimless crime”. Is anyone actually hurt by the presence of tampons in school bathrooms? I doubt it. Is it a little strange to place them in boys bathrooms? Yes. But “a little strange” isn’t the same as “harmful”.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which historical event or story left you most amazed?
Answer: One of my favorite stories is probably that of Theodore “Teddy” Roosevelt. A small, sickly and asthmatic child, he wasn’t expected to live long or amount to much. And through sheer force of will, he molded himself into a tough guy — he took up boxing, wrestling, horseback riding, shooting. Left his comfortable, well-off New York lifestyle to become a cattle rancher at 20. If you saw the lad at ten and saw him again just ten years later, you wouldn’t believe how much he changed, and kept changing. He called his lifestyle “The Strenuous Life”, and summed it up thus: I wish to preach, not the doctrine of ignoble ease, but the doctrine of the strenuous life, the life of toil and effort, of labor and strife; to preach that highest form of success which comes, not to the man who desires mere easy peace, but to the man who does not shrink from danger, from hardship, or from bitter toil, and who out of these wins the splendid ultimate triumph. Roosevelt was a conservationist, founder of national parks, protector of nature and while he was a fighter, a warrior, a brawler and a military man for much of his pre-presidential life, he would later brag with some pride that during his time in office “not a single shot was fired”. Every week, even as a governor and president, Roosevelt would spar with random people in private boxing matches. Once he got hit so hard he lost sight in his left eye — he didn’t tell a soul. Another time someone tried to assassinate him during a speech. Roosevelt was hit in the chest and still finished the speech. Going from a sickly rich boy in New York to the absolute beast of a man he ended up becoming is one of history’s most amazing transformations.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: If Trump wins, would his presidency be a challenge not only for Ukraine, but for Russia too?
Answer: Lets assume for a moment that he wins. And he does somehow end the Ukraine war, like he said he would. End it in such a way that is advantageous to Russia more than to Ukraine. Now here’s the thing — the ‘eternal war’ scenario kind of causes Russia’s economy to boom somewhat. A war economy makes for many new jobs in weapons factories.[1] Other areas, meanwhile, are severely neglected. Now let us assume Trump was sworn in. Forces Ukraine to the table. By December, the war is over. Russia now has to rebuild its economy. But it is still under sanctions. Putin and his cronies are still war criminals who cannot travel much of the world. And millions of young Russian men that left during the first year of the war out of fear of being sent to the trenches, are now comfortably living and settled abroad. Will they come back to Russia, a land with an economy that’s largely dying aside from their military industrial complex? Doubtful. If anything, the ongoing war keeps Russia afloat economically and masks just how bad things have gotten. A sudden end to the war would very likely mark the end of Russia itself, as well. And unlike Ukraine, Russia would not be able to count on the world’s sympathy in rebuilding itself. Honestly, for now and the foreseeable future, the status quo of ongoing warfare and increased war-time production is as good as it gets for Russia.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Who do you think is or was the most bizarre person in the world?
Answer: Perhaps not the most bizarre, but definitely a wonderfully eccentric contender to the title… a Japanese general by the name of Count Nagaoka Gaishi. Gaishi was known as a great military leader, some having dubbed him the “father of Japanese aviation”. Above all, he was known for his enormous moustache — it was reportedly the largest moustache not only in the Japanese imperial army, but in all of the world. In 1933, Gaishi did the very thing that all men must one day do — he died, aged 74. Bladder cancer did the magnificently moustachio’d generalissmo in. The family got together and decided to take a rather unusual step; they built not one, but two graves. In one grave on the traditional burial mound, his family buried the old general. His eldest son then carefully removed the count’s enormous moustache with clippers. And the moustache was buried in another grave, nearby.[1] One of Count Gaishi’s graves, above. One contained his ashes — he was cremated, as per his wishes. The other contains a smaller casket with, in it, the mighty ‘stache. It is wrapped in white silk for posterity. Those who wish to pay hommage to the greatest moustache of Japanese history but refuse to honor its military, may travel to Fujiyama and do so.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Is “toxic masculinity” a scam to turn men into beta males?
Answer: First of all, no truly “manly man” will use terms like “beta males” without a hint of irony. So please, drop that… it’s unbecoming of a gentleman. Makes you look like a whiny little no-lifer. Now as for this whole toxic masculinity business, it’s largely bullshit. I mean sure — some of the expectations we have of men aren’t fair, and are hard to live up to. We should go a little easier on men, at times. Go a little easier on ourselves, too. But does showing kindness to men mean we should coddle people, that we should embrace weakness, overly emotional responses, and hysterics, and label them a virtue? Because not keeping a cool head under pressure isn’t a virtue. Getting down and dirty to earn a living and taking a beating and fight back like man, THAT is a virtue. Life chews us all up, and spits us out. And yes, it sucks. But what goes ever did crying about it, to anyone? No, I’m not of the belief that “everything used to be better”. Because objectively, that hasn’t been true for most of history. But there’s way too much posturing, too much hysterics, too much whiny attention grabbing and too many “think pieces” from people who never had an original thought pop up into their heads — and half of them contain buzzwords like “toxic masculinity” or “the patriarchy”. Much of the ‘social commentary’ today from people who studies this type of thing (yes, there are studies…) boil down to “straight men bad, especially white ones, everyone else pitiful and oppressed”. It’s tiresome as hell. The constant hammering on “toxic masculinity”, the constant complaining about “men are trash”, the constant barrage of feminist buzzwords all across social media by people who couldn’t coherently explain even a third of their theories… it’s too much. Men are amazing. We’re glorious, powerful creatures. We are half of this earth’s population, most of our leaders are men, our great and powerful historical figures, our icons, the authors of our holy books. Enough with the neverending quest to shame men for being men — all that does is drive them into the ‘other camp’ where they’ll embrace false Gods like Andrew Tate.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Should the world accept the "non binary " gender?
Answer: It’s just the sort of non-issue people want you to argue about… the Supreme Court in America just made the office President into that of semi-King…[1] Meanwhile? The man most likely to win in November according to all polls, is compromised by both China and Russia and may well be a foreign asset.[2] And here you are… asking about “non-binary” genders… Gender is… a very personal thing. I used to argue about it, from time to time. Even get into debates about it. But all this “culture war” nonsense really is nothing but a distraction in the grand scheme of things. The world is teetering on the brink of WWIII. Environmental protection laws are at risk of being hollowed out, corruption is at an all-time high and at risk of becoming even higher in years to come. There’s plastic in EVERYTHING, and it’s literally slowly making us all infertile.[3] And yet here we are. Talking about made-up gender identities that help no one, and honestly harm no one, either. Just, live and let live. And focus on those things that are killing us, rather than allowing ourselves to be distracted by silly nonsense while a gathering storm approaches…

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: How do you think history will judge Donald Trump's handling of the assassination attempt?
Answer: He’s the most image-conscious man alive today. Years of being in reality television has taught him well. So he knew immediately after being shot, that he could not cower. Could not appear weak. Not for even a second. So there’s that defiant fist-pump. And it’s dumb, in that moment — he’s making himself to be an even bigger target. Had there been a second shooter, this could have been a perfect time to take out Trump with a second, well-timed bullet… But he doesn’t care. He’s got the Devil’s luck and he’s completely confident that he will survive. And in that moment, all that matters to Trump? Image. So he played his cards. He wrestled against his own security team, stood up, and raised his fist. Face bloodied. Lips mouthing: “Fight! Fight! Fight!” Because he’s a fighter. He wants to be seen as one. As that Churchillian bulldog. The John Wayne. The unbendable, unbreakable, conquering hero. A man whose ego is truly larger than his sense of self-preservation. And in that moment, he was brave. Foolish, but brave. He released a statement, too. And it was remarkably measured. Calm. Not fiery, not passionate, not unhinged… but it read, for the first time in a long time, like the statement of a man who has listened to advisors. And has toned down his rhetoric somewhat. Time will tell if this will remain the case. It is known that President Joe Biden reached out to former President Trump the very same evening, and that the two men talked. Biden’s team even pulled some of the strongest anti-Trump ads off the television. It was a remarkable show of (relative) unity in a divided country. One that caught me by surprise to tell you the truth. What will history remember? It depends entirely on how the next days and weeks play out. Goodwill won is lost easily with a few ill-timed statements or actions. Trump could use the attack to his benefit in the campaign. And the Democrats, meanwhile, will keep hammering the fact that the shooter was a registered Republican gun-nut who used the same automatic assault rifle their party had wanted to ban for civilian use… which narrative will win? We’ll find out on November. Now, to use Trump’s own words after a school shooting in Iowa six months prior: “Get over it!”[1]

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Macron has called for a new election in light of his party's election defeat in EU elections in 2024. Will Marine Le Penn become the French President, and what will its repercussions for France and the rest of the EU?
Answer: The breaking news right now — the far-right won in France. Emmanuel Macron’s high stakes gamble did NOT pay off, and his party massively lost in the snap election he called to re-establish his grip on power… the far-right won handily. Second-highest number of votes went to the far-left, instead. And Macron’s more centrist liberal party got demolished. To say the outcome of this election is a complete and utter political earthquake of historical proportions, would be an understatement. France’s Macron was Mister Europe, very strongly pro-European Union. The far-right is NOT. Neither is the far-left. There will be another round, on July 7. But this is huge. France is a firm supporter of Ukraine, one of Europe’s strongest military forces and a major player within NATO. The new guys? They hate Ukraine, love Russia, hate Brussels and are of the Brexit-variety… These guys who won? They’re like the Nigel Farage’s, the Wilders’ of France. Or for you Yankees out there — the French MAGAs. Given the pivotal role France has historically played inside the European Union, this election result will cause a seismic shift within Europe. The consequences of this election will be felt the world over. Europe’s far-right has never been this powerful in decades.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Are celebrities actually nice?
Answer: Some of them are, some of them aren’t… kind of like with ‘normal people’. James Gandolfini is a fine example of a celebrity who was a genuinely nice in real life. While playing on The Sopranos, he was fiercely protective and paternal towards his on-screen daughter, Jamie-Lynn Sigler. She was diagnosed with muscle disease MS on the show, and it devastated her. Sigler didn’t tell any of her castmates of the diagnosis, and no one asked… she would have dizzy spells, muscle pains, and have to take many bathroom breaks during scenes as the disease affected her bladder — no one would bothered to ask, everyone just got grumpy as her health interrupted filming. Gandolfini was the only person who asked “are you okay?” and Sigler told him of her illness. She asked him not to tell anyone — and he didn’t.[1] He just quietly helped her get through it. It wasn’t until Gandolfini’s death, ten years later, that Sigler found out something else about him… for over a decade, without telling anyone, he had been giving generous donations to foundations aimed at fighting the disease his co-star suffered from. A genuinely good person does good quietly — kindness requires no accolades.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Was Hitler really 5.9" tall?
Answer: Yes, he was. People like to pretend he was much smaller, or that he was a weak or boring guy who couldn’t get laid or whatever, but that’s just a coping mechanism from people who feel compelled to demean Hitler from the great beyond. Below, we see him with Paul von Hindenburg. Von Hindenburg was a very tall man for his era and stood about 6′4″ in his prime. In the photo above, he likely lost some height — Von Hindenburg is, after all, already in his eighties and by the time we reach our eighties, we have typically lost a few inches of height. And while Hitler is noticeably shorter, he’s not that much shorter. Looking at the height of both men’s shoulders, the height difference is at best a few inches. I’d say Hitler was definitely around 5′9″, at least at this point in life. By the time he died he was stooped over, feeble from bad medications and Parkinson’s disease and likely a bit shorter, maybe around 5′8″ or even as short as 5′7″. I’d say Adolf Hitler was about 5′9″ at his peak. Not a tall man, but not a short man for his era, either. Mao was about 5′11″ in his prime. The whole “dictators are tiny insecure men” spiel is kind of… bullshit. Julius Caesar was a tall man, even Napoleon was perfectly average for his era. It’s silly to try and reduce people to stereotypes like “haha he was a gay midget with one testicle”. Doesn’t help anyone.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Which historical figure made a situation worse than it already was?
Answer: A fine example would be Robert Mugabe. He started off as an anti-colonialist rebel, took over control of the country and, initially, made some decent reforms in Zimbabwe. Then he decided that he “must be like Hitler”… Hitler was strong, Mugabe argued. He “stood for his people” and if standing up for your own race is to be like Hitler, he said, “he would be like Hitler tenfold” and even grew the moustache to prove it. Robert Mugabe, the self-described “anti-Racist” then began taking away lands from white farmers, giving them to black farmers. They primarily went, of course, to those people he was already close to — distant relatives, friends, allies and members of his tribe. This proved disastrous for Zimbabwe as incompetent new owners would sell expensive farming equipment for a quick buck, leading to food production to plummet and the economy to take a major hit. Mugabe stayed in power from 1980 until the day he was deposed in 2017, aged 93. He went from strong nationalist leader to an incompetent buffoon clinging to control, whose shameless nepotism drove his country into the abyss. Proving once again that age old wisdom — when someone openly admired Hitler and sports a Hitler stache, he probably isn’t a good dude.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What is the white savior complex, and what are some classic examples of it?
Answer: When one has a “white savior complex”, a white person believes him or herself to be a great beacon of morality — the person showcases a strange mixture of both inferiority (hates their own whiteness) and superiority (knows more about oppression than the oppressed, themselves). A fine example is the case of a Dutchman named Thomas van Beersum. He was a 22-year-old Communist activist from the Netherlands who, in 2013, joined an anti-government protest in Manila, the Philippines. Thomas van Beersum, the young white Communist, is shown berating a member of the Filipino riot police. Telling him he’s a disgrace, a shame to his own country, an oppressor and “an agent of neo-colonialism”. Thomas knows better than the Filipino policeman — he’s enlightened, he’s woke, he’s an activist! The policeman eventually broke into tears from all the verbal abuse and shaming he received.[1] The Philippines identified Van Beersum, took his fingerprints and banished him from the country. He was declared “persona non grata” and told never ever to return.[2] Thomas van Beersum had ties to exiled NPA leader Joma Sison. Sison, whose NPA (New People’s Army) is a designated terrorist organization, had radicaled the young Dutch man.[3] To the point where he felt he knew better than those “poor misguided brown people” in the Philippines. The radical communist ‘friends’ of Thomas kill Filipino soldiers and policemen each year. He no doubt believes they have it coming — they’re all “oppressors”. Thomas knows better. The “white savior complex” is a powerful drug. It’s behind the movement to name Latino people “Latinx” and Filipino “Filipinx” because Filipina or Latina is a “gendered term”. It is behind things like a young white activist berating a policeman just doing his job to the point of tears. Because the young white activist knows best — better than Latino people, better than black or Asian people. He knows best, because he’s white. He invented ‘oppression’ and now only through him, enlightened one, salvation can come.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: Why is Islam the most toxic religion in the world?
Answer: It’s kind of a tiresome line of reasoning, and not one I am very fond of. As far as criticism goes, Islam gets its fair share — and rightfully so. But it’s “low-hanging fruit” where I’m concerned. Take for instance Mormons. Below we see a photo of a group of Mormon polygamists imprisoned in a facility in Utah, in 1889. Islam limits men to a maximum of four wives — and they may only marry a second, third or fourth wife if they are financially well-off enough to provide the same lifestyle for the additional wives as they can the first and primary wife. They must treat these wives well, and have relatively relaxed divorce laws compared to some other faiths. By contrast, some Mormon sects allowed, and still allow, their male faithful to marry a near endless amount of women. I once read the grandfather of Mitt Romey was a polygamist and has tens of thousands of descendants alive today… We can single out Islam. Barbaric, backwards, treats women like cattle… Go ahead ahead. It’s your prerogative. But let us not delude ourselves — religion, in general, has a pretty lousy track records where it comes to human rights. Furthermore, there’s no such thing as one universal Islam; there are some Muslim nations that are quite liberal, and some that are incredibly regressive. My best friend married a Malaysian Muslima who smokes, drinks and hasn’t worn a hijab in ages.

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What actors in a film have the strongest resemblance to the actual people depicted?
Answer: Billy Zane will portray Marlon Brando in an upcoming Brando biopic called Waltzing with Brando. Zane will portray the famous actor, activist, inventor and Lothario in the late 1960s and early 1970s, when he starred in the Godfather and acquired his tropical getaway in Tahiti. The resemblance between the two men is incredibly strong — Zane looks nearly identical to a middle-aged Brando, in the years before the massive weight gain of his later life. I’m quite interested in the film, because the figure of Brando is quite compelling… he lived quite a life. Even in the biographies of other famous people, he’ll often show up out nowhere. Such as Keith Richard’s Life, where Brando briefly ‘steals’ his first wife from Richards and “reads poetry to her” (wink-wink) before returnijng her to the Rolling Stone guitarist. Even the way Brando acquired his island, Tetiaroa, is fascinating — he purchased it from an elderly lady who lived on the island alone. She had inherited it from her father, a dentist who helped out the last reigning King of Tahiti, Pōmare V. It was during the shooting of “Mutiny on the Bounty” that Brando felt paradise on earth was to live in a tropical island, be by the beach, and just never leave. He was King of his domain, there. Had quite the harem going, too. In a Playboy interview, in the 1970s, Brando takes a reporter snorkeling. A giant shark approaches — Brando turns around, punches it on the snout and it takes off in a hurry. I’ve been waiting for a biopic on this man for ages. It’s high time he gets one, and in Zane we find a fine lookalike, who also happens to be an excellent actor. Will be good!

Name: Jean-Marie Valheur
Question: What epic moment in history did you witness?
Answer: I’d like you to imagine a city of seven million souls, rising up almost as one. One day out seven million people, two million are out in the streets. It was eerie. Schools were empty. Shops closed. Students marching alongside teachers. Police officers, nurses, elderly grandparents hoisting granchildren onto their shoulders… words don’t really do justice to the sheer size of the 2019–2020 Hong Kong protests. Nor do pictures fully capture the massiveness of the seas of people gathered there… You’d be anywhere in the city away from the mass of protesters, and you would be struck by how… empty it was. Like a post-apocalyptic scene. It seemed as if almost everyone was out there, at first. Of course the authorities did all they could to lessen turnout, to thwart protesters and eventually beat them down by any means necessary. And as the months went by, crowd sizes went down significantly. But nothing I’ve ever seen will compare to those first days of protest. It was a whole city coming together as one soul. Speaking with what seemed like one voice. And saying, loud and clear: “We do NOT want to be a part of China and fall under China’s corrupt jurisdiction!” We all know what happened. How the protests were crushed and how — conveniently — Covid-19 arrived just around that time. Suddenly ‘mass gatherings’ were forbidden altogether. For public health reasons, the authorities said. Hong Kong had been promised autonomy and the right to elect its own leadership until the year 2047, but Xi callously rolled back all promises and brought the city-state to heel. A vibrant culture was crushed overnight. But I was there to see it’s defiant last stand. And it was spectacular.
